evidence_row: Moderate certainty evidence from multiple systematic reviews , benefits considered to outweigh harms (adverse events for these interventions are mild and would not mitigate their use, although concerns been raised that varenicline may slightly increase cardiovascular events in people already at increased risk of those illnesses).

population: tobacco use in all adults and young people
text: refer people who want to stop smoking to local stop smoking support , preferably where behavioural support and prescribed stop smoking medicines are available.
evidence_row: Moderate certainty evidence. NICE guidance supports this recommendation as ‘evidence and expert opinion showed that support provided by these services is clinically effective and highly cost-effective in helping people to stop smoking’ .

population: tobacco use in all adults and young people
text: Acknowledge that e-cigarettes may be helpful for some smokers for quitting or reducing smoking.
evidence_row: Recommendation based on low certainty evidence from one systematic review; insufficient evidence to demonstrate the long-term effects .

population: Smokeless tobacco use in all adults and young people
text: Ask patients if they use smokeless tobacco, using the names that the various products are known by locally. It may be helpful to show a picture of what the products look like (see chapter 11, figure 1).
evidence_row: Recommendation: moderate certainty evidence evaluating tobacco cessation in dental settings and the effectiveness of brief opportunistic smoking cessation interventions . Guidance on showing pictures of what products look like presented in NICE guidance .

population: Smokeless tobacco use in all adults and young people
text: If someone uses smokeless tobacco, ensure they are aware of the health risks and provide very brief advice.
evidence_row: Moderate certainty evidence underpinning this NICE guidance statement .

population: Smokeless tobacco use in all adults and young people
text: Refer patients who want to quit to specialist support services.
evidence_row: Based on moderate certainty evidence ‘that support provided by these services is clinically effective and highly cost-effective in helping people to stop smoking’ .

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people
text: Use the AUDIT-C tool (or similar) to assess a patient’s level of risk of alcohol harm by completing 3 consumption questions.
evidence_row: Recommendation based on moderate certainty evidence from a systematic review showed that brief interventions can reduce alcohol consumption in those drinking hazardous or harmful amounts of alcohol when compared to minimal or no interventions .

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people
text: If AUDIT C score is 4 or below, give positive feedback and encourage your patient to keep their drinking at lower risk levels.

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people
text: If score is 5 to 10, give brief advice to encourage a reduction in alcohol consumption and reduce the risk of alcohol harm.

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people
text: Feed back to the patient that their level of drinking is putting them at risk of developing a range of health problems (including cancers of the mouth, throat and breast) and this increases the more you drink and the more frequently you drink.

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people

text: For those who are pregnant or think they could become pregnant, the safest approach is not to drink alcohol at all, to remove the risk of alcohol-related harm to the baby.
evidence_row: A well conducted systematic review highlights the paucity of evidence evaluating light drinking in pregnancy compared with abstinence .  Based on this research, the CMO’s guidance supports a ‘precautionary’ approach .

population: alcohol use in all adults and young people
text: AUDIT-C score of 11 or above, refer to GP or community specialist alcohol service.

population: diet
text: Promote increased consumption of non-starchy vegetables and fruit
evidence_row: Most of the evidence underpinning recommendations concerning diet and cancer prevention comes from observational studies and laboratory or animal studies and is considered low certainty. text: It’s not recommended to use vital staining, oral cytology or light‐based detection and/or oral spectroscopy for evaluating lesions for malignancy.
evidence_row: Recommendation based on moderate certainty evidence from a well conducted systematic review of diagnostic accuracy of index tests for the detection of oral cancer and potentially malignant disorders of the lip and oral cavity, in patients presenting with clinically evident lesions .

text: Obtain an updated medical, social and dental history and perform an intraoral and extraoral visual and tactile examination for all patients at each oral health assessment visit.

text: Maintain good dietary practice in line with the Eatwell Guide including avoiding or minimising sugar sweetened drinks (especially carbonated) and fruit juice and/or smoothies (limited to 150ml per day).
